name: Tree-covered footprint beside London Hall
summary: Tree-covered footprint beside London Hall is a small rectangular footprint covered by branches beside the service drive, tentatively represented as a low enclosure of uncertain use.

evidence.note: Tree canopy covers the full outlined area. No roof edge can be traced independently of the rectangular municipal footprint. Colours are estimates.

Regional 2 m grid, heights above local ground. Median 12.62 m, P90 13.05 m, maximum 13.2 m. The 13 m return is continuous with the adjacent tree crown and unsupported by any photograph of a tall building.
Automatic match looks at the London Hall lobby. It supplies no identifiable facade for this footprint.
Drive view between the residences shows trees in the sightline.
The end of the forecourt is screened by vegetation and there is no distinct tall wall.

notes: Presence of a roof under the tree, use, wall material and height are unconfirmed. The low enclosure is a provisional interpretation of the city outline.
lidarNote: The lidar measures an overhanging tree crown. Provisional height comes from the scale of adjacent service enclosures.
